intro: A Venn diagram shows groups as circles. A circle inside another means everything in the small group is also in the big one; overlapping circles mean some things are in both; circles apart mean nothing is in both. Work out how every pair of groups is related, then find the diagram where every pair of circles sits the same way.

tips.title: Three ways two groups can sit
tips.body: Every pair of groups is one of three: one inside the other (every dog is an animal), overlapping (some doctors are women), or apart (no pen is a tree).
tips.caption: Inside: all of one group is in the other. Overlap: some are in both. Apart: none are in both.

tips.title: Check every pair
tips.body: Three groups make three pairs; four groups make six. A diagram is right only if every pair of circles sits the way its groups do. Cross a diagram out as soon as one pair is wrong.

tips.title: One thing in two groups
tips.body: If one thing belongs to two groups (C.V. Raman is a scientist and a Nobel prize winner), its circle goes inside both, where the two circles overlap.

tips.title: Counting in a Venn diagram
tips.body: “Coffee” means the whole coffee circle, including the part it shares with tea: 30 + 20 = 50. “Only tea” is the part of the tea circle outside coffee. “Both” is the overlap.

tips.title: Size doesn't matter
tips.body: A small circle does not mean a small group. Only how the circles sit matters: inside, overlapping or apart.
